title: Weekly AI & Agentic Systems Digest — November 8–14, 2026
summary: This week tightened the production boundary around agent execution: AgentCore added direct web retrieval, changed its default runtime, and widened OAuth compatibility; MCP patched command-execution and confinement vulnerabilities; Google introduced a typed decision API; and OpenAI’s Agents SDK alpha expanded durable state, budgets, hosted tools, and Agent2Agent support.

developments.title: AgentCore adds a direct Web Search API
developments.availability: Available in six AWS Regions through AWS SDKs and the AWS CLI, with IAM authorization, PrivateLink access, CloudTrail data events, and pricing of $7 per 1,000 queries.
developments.what_changed: The new InvokeWebSearch API returns ranked web results without requiring an AgentCore Gateway resource. Results include an extract and, when available, title, URL, and publication time; requests can filter by domain and publication time.
developments.why_it_matters: Applications can now use AgentCore’s raw web index directly instead of choosing between a Gateway MCP tool and a synthesized Web Answer response.
developments.platform_impact: This creates a cleaner retrieval primitive for custom agent loops and evidence pipelines, while IAM, network access, audit events, source policy, prompt-injection handling, and downstream synthesis remain application concerns.
developments.recommended_action: Run a frozen comparison of direct Web Search, Web Answer, and the current retrieval stack on source coverage, result freshness, injection resistance, latency, and completed-answer cost.
developments.watchouts: The launch is regional and usage-priced. Raw search results still require source-quality evaluation, content handling, and claim-to-evidence validation.

developments.title: AgentCore Runtime V2 becomes the default for new runtimes
developments.availability: Default for newly created runtimes in 19 listed AWS Regions; existing runtimes remain on their current version unless explicitly updated.
developments.what_changed: AWS changed the next-generation AgentCore Runtime from an explicit opt-in to the default for new runtimes in 19 Regions. Operators can select platformVersion V2 for migration or V1 to retain the previous generation for a new runtime.
developments.why_it_matters: A default change affects deployment assumptions even when teams do not start a deliberate migration project.
developments.platform_impact: Runtime version must become an explicit infrastructure setting with startup, memory, image, concurrency, session-isolation, billing, and rollback tests. Existing runtime fleets will otherwise become mixed-version estates.
developments.recommended_action: Inventory runtime versions, pin platformVersion in infrastructure code, and replay one production-like workload on V1 and V2 before migrating existing runtimes.
developments.watchouts: AWS reports sub-two-second P75 startup for a tested 2 GB image and up to 68% less billed memory for multi-turn agents; these figures are workload-specific vendor measurements.
developments.new_delta: Since the September 22 issue, Runtime V2 changed from an explicit opt-in in five launch Regions to the default for new runtimes in 19 Regions.

developments.title: MCP reference servers v2.4.0 patch six vulnerabilities
developments.availability: Patched packages are @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem 2.3.0 and mcp-server-git plus mcp-server-fetch 2026.11.11.
developments.what_changed: Version 2.4.0 fixes six vulnerabilities across the filesystem, Git, and fetch reference servers. A high-severity Git flaw allowed an untrusted repository’s own configuration to execute a program during nominally read-only operations such as git_status; other fixes address filesystem races, repository-confinement bypasses, IPv6 SSRF filtering, and robots.txt path handling.
developments.why_it_matters: Read-only tool labels did not prevent process execution, showing that repository metadata and implementation behavior can cross the intended agent capability boundary.
developments.platform_impact: MCP inventory and patching must cover server packages, host Git versions, filesystem semantics, network parsing, and trusted repository origins—not only gateway allowlists and tool descriptions.
developments.recommended_action: Patch every affected MCP server, then add a regression using an untrusted repository with hostile Git configuration plus path, symlink, redirect, IPv6, and private-network cases.
developments.watchouts: The release documents residual Windows junction and race limitations. The filesystem package’s semantic version can also sort below older calendar-version packages, so upgrades should pin the exact patched version.
developments.new_delta: Since the November 7 issue covered v2.3.0 confinement controls, v2.4.0 fixes six newly disclosed vulnerabilities, including command execution through an untrusted repository’s Git configuration.

developments.title: AgentCore Identity adds OAuth 2.0 discovery URLs
developments.availability: Available for inbound JWT authorizers and outbound custom OAuth credential providers in Regions where AgentCore is available.
developments.what_changed: AgentCore Identity can now use OAuth 2.0 authorization-server metadata URLs as well as OpenID Connect discovery URLs. Previously, authorization servers that implemented OAuth 2.0 without OIDC could not be configured through discovery metadata.
developments.why_it_matters: The change expands compatibility with enterprise authorization servers without requiring teams to misrepresent them as OIDC providers or hand-wire endpoint metadata.
developments.platform_impact: Identity integration tests should verify issuer and endpoint metadata, key rotation, token audience, inbound validation, outbound credential flows, and failure behavior rather than treating discovery success as authorization correctness.
developments.recommended_action: Connect one non-OIDC OAuth authorization server in a sandbox and test metadata refresh, key rotation, invalid issuer and audience values, unavailable endpoints, and revoked credentials.
developments.watchouts: Metadata discovery improves compatibility but does not validate an authorization design, token scope, policy mapping, or revocation path by itself.

developments.title: Google releases Gemini Decision 1 and the Decisions API
developments.availability: Available through the Gemini Developer API v1beta with Gemini Decision 1; the guide documents text and multimodal shared inputs but excludes conversation-history, tool-call, context-caching, Batch, Flex, and Priority-inference paths.
developments.what_changed: The Decisions API evaluates typed yes/no, choice, and ordered-score questions and returns probabilities and confidence instead of generated prose. Google states that it produces zero output tokens and can evaluate independent questions over shared text, PDF, audio, image, or video input.
developments.why_it_matters: It makes probabilistic routing, scoring, and escalation a distinct API primitive rather than a prompt that generates JSON for application code to parse.
developments.platform_impact: Bedrock-centered teams can test the same architecture with classifiers or constrained model calls: keep thresholds, authorization, and composite policy deterministic while treating model confidence as an input rather than a decision authority.
developments.recommended_action: Build a 500-case calibration set for one routing or escalation decision and compare probability calibration, false automation, abstention rate, latency, and cost with the current generative classifier.
developments.watchouts: The API is v1beta, and calibrated probabilities still require workload-specific calibration. Confidence must not directly grant permissions or approve irreversible actions.

developments.title: OpenAI Agents SDK alpha expands durable execution and interoperability
developments.availability: Published as the prerelease openai-agents-python v0.24.0-alpha.7; it is not a stable production release.
developments.what_changed: The alpha adds application-owned durable root sessions, reconciliation for uncertain tool effects, hosted File Search, Code Interpreter and Image Generation tools, context and completion hooks, observed-usage budgets, expanded MCP resources and prompts, native Agent2Agent adapters, and local execution. It also changes new environment write policy to strict and renames MCP approval modes.
developments.why_it_matters: The release exposes concrete design choices for durable state, side-effect recovery, budget admission, tool governance, and cross-agent interoperability that can be compared with AgentCore and Bedrock Managed Agents.
developments.platform_impact: Teams testing the SDK need checkpoint compatibility, executor-policy, approval-mode, usage-accounting, child-agent, and hosted-tool regression coverage before upgrading alpha environments.
developments.recommended_action: Use a disposable project to test session resume after an uncertain tool result, strict write boundaries, budget overrun behavior, MCP approvals, and one A2A exchange; do not migrate production workflows from the alpha alone.
developments.watchouts: The release is prerelease and contains breaking configuration changes. Its budgets are admission controls: an admitted request can exceed a limit, and child usage is excluded.

devops_impacts.text: Separate raw retrieval, synthesized answers, and typed decisions into explicit services with distinct evidence, latency, cost, and failure contracts.
Pin AgentCore platformVersion and MCP package versions explicitly; defaults and package ordering can otherwise change runtime or security posture without an obvious application diff.
Treat repository metadata, OAuth discovery, local executors, redirects, network addresses, and filesystem behavior as executable trust boundaries outside the model prompt.

Record retrieval sources, serving runtime version, policy and identity decisions, tool side effects, budget admission, and model confidence so failures can be reconstructed without trusting generated explanations.
Compare completed-task economics across direct search, synthesis, decision calls, runtime memory, and agent retries; request prices and vendor efficiency claims do not show total workflow cost.

bring_to_work.title: Retrieval boundary bake-off
bring_to_work.what: Compare direct AgentCore Web Search, Web Answer, and the existing retrieval pipeline on a fixed current-information set.
bring_to_work.fit: Direct fit for Bedrock and AgentCore applications that need current external evidence.
bring_to_work.next_step: Freeze 50 questions and score coverage, freshness, citation alignment, injection failures, p95 latency, and cost per supported answer.

bring_to_work.title: Runtime version control
bring_to_work.what: Make AgentCore runtime generation an explicit, tested infrastructure choice.
bring_to_work.fit: Direct fit for any AgentCore Runtime fleet or CI/CD path that creates new runtimes.
bring_to_work.next_step: Inventory versions, pin platformVersion, replay one representative workload on V1 and V2, and document rollback.

bring_to_work.title: MCP hostile-repository regression
bring_to_work.what: Verify that read-only Git tools cannot execute repository-controlled programs or escape repository and network boundaries.
bring_to_work.fit: Direct fit for AgentCore Gateway or any agent runtime exposing MCP Git, filesystem, or fetch servers.
bring_to_work.next_step: Patch exact versions, then run hostile .git/config, alternates, symlink or junction, redirect, IPv6, and private-address cases in isolation.

bring_to_work.title: Decision calibration pilot
bring_to_work.what: Evaluate typed probabilistic decisions against the current generative routing prompt.
bring_to_work.fit: Transferable to Bedrock stacks for routing, escalation, moderation, and evaluation even though Google’s API is external.
bring_to_work.next_step: Label 500 cases and compare calibration error, false automation, abstention, latency, and cost; keep authorization deterministic.

watchouts.text: AgentCore Web Search is available in six listed Regions and costs $7 per 1,000 queries; source trust and downstream synthesis remain the application’s responsibility.
Runtime V2 performance and memory figures are AWS measurements on stated test conditions, not guarantees for a specific image, tool chain, model call, or traffic pattern.
MCP v2.4.0 requires exact package upgrades and still documents residual Windows junction and race limitations; read-only naming is not a security boundary.
The Decisions API is v1beta, while OpenAI Agents SDK v0.24.0-alpha.7 is prerelease; both require bounded evaluation before they influence production control paths.

telegram_text:
# Weekly AI & Agentic Systems Digest — November 8–14, 2026

The week’s pattern was explicit production boundaries: AgentCore separated raw web retrieval from synthesized answers, changed the default runtime, and widened OAuth compatibility; MCP patched vulnerabilities that crossed supposedly read-only tool boundaries; Google introduced typed probabilistic decisions; and OpenAI’s Agents SDK alpha expanded durable execution controls.

## What changed

**1. AgentCore added a direct Web Search API.** *Shipped — GA, November 10.* `InvokeWebSearch` returns ranked results without requiring a Gateway resource, including an extract and, when available, title, URL, and publication time. Requests support domain and publication-time filters; access uses IAM, PrivateLink is supported, and calls can be logged as CloudTrail data events. Pricing is $7 per 1,000 queries in six listed Regions. [AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/11/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-web-search-api/)[1]

This is a lower-level retrieval boundary than last week’s Web Answer launch: applications can own evidence selection and synthesis rather than receiving a managed synthesized answer.[1]

**2. AgentCore Runtime V2 became the default for new runtimes.** *Shipped — GA, November 12.* New runtimes use V2 by default in 19 Regions; existing runtimes stay on their current generation until explicitly updated. Teams can set `platformVersion=V2` for migration or `V1` for a new runtime that must retain the previous generation. [AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/11/new-agentcore-runtime-default/)[2] [AWS technical detail](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/run-agents-securely-and-efficiently-with-the-next-generation-agentcore-runtime/)[3]

Since the September 22 issue, V2 moved from an opt-in launch in five Regions to the default for new runtimes in 19. Runtime generation should now be pinned in infrastructure code rather than inherited from a service default.[2][3]

**3. MCP reference servers v2.4.0 patched six vulnerabilities.** *Open-sourced/published, November 11.* The most consequential flaw let an untrusted repository’s Git configuration execute a program during nominally read-only operations such as `git_status`. Other fixes cover filesystem races, repository-confinement bypasses, IPv6 server-side request forgery filtering, and `robots.txt` path handling. Patched targets are filesystem 2.3.0 and Git/fetch 2026.11.11. [Release](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/releases/tag/v2.4.0)[5] [Advisory](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/security/advisories/GHSA-6hqx-gqrx-c5r2)[6]

This is a material delta from last week’s confinement controls: a read-only tool description did not prevent execution through repository metadata.[5][6]

**4. AgentCore Identity added OAuth 2.0 discovery URLs.** *Shipped — GA, November 13.* Inbound JWT authorizers and outbound custom OAuth credential providers can now use OAuth 2.0 authorization-server metadata, not only OpenID Connect discovery. [AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/11/bedrock-agentcore-oauth2-discovery/)[4]

The change expands enterprise identity-provider compatibility, but metadata discovery still needs issuer, audience, scope, key-rotation, revocation, and failure-path tests.[4]

**5. Google released Gemini Decision 1 and the Decisions API.** *Shipped — v1beta, November 11.* The API answers typed yes/no, choice, and ordered-score questions with probabilities and confidence rather than generated prose. Google says it produces zero output tokens and accepts shared text, PDF, audio, image, or video input. [Changelog](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog.md.txt)[7] [Guide](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/decisions-api)[8]

This is an architectural signal for Bedrock teams: routing, scoring, and escalation can be modeled as probabilistic classification with deterministic thresholds instead of JSON-generating prompts. Confidence must remain an input—not authorization.[7][8]

**6. OpenAI Agents SDK v0.24.0-alpha.7 expanded durable execution and interoperability.** *Open-sourced prerelease, November 8.* The alpha adds application-owned durable root sessions, uncertain-tool-effect reconciliation, hosted tools, context and completion hooks, usage budgets, expanded MCP resources and prompts, native Agent2Agent adapters, and local execution. It also introduces breaking defaults, including strict write policy for new environments and renamed MCP approval modes. [Release](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/tag/v0.24.0-alpha.7)[9]

The design is useful comparison material for AgentCore and Bedrock Managed Agents, but the prerelease label and breaking configuration changes argue against production migration.[9]

## DevOps / platform impact

- **Architecture:** Separate raw retrieval, synthesis, and typed decisions into explicit services with distinct evidence, latency, cost, and failure contracts.[1][7][8]
- **Deployment:** Pin AgentCore `platformVersion` and exact MCP package versions; defaults and version ordering can otherwise change runtime or security posture without an application-code diff.[2][5]
- **Security:** Treat repository metadata, OAuth discovery, local executors, redirects, network addresses, and filesystem semantics as executable trust boundaries outside the prompt layer.[4][5][9]
- **Observability:** Record retrieval sources, runtime generation, identity and policy decisions, tool side effects, budget admission, and confidence values so failures can be reconstructed.[1][2][9]
- **Cost:** Measure completed-task economics across search, synthesis, decision calls, runtime memory, and retries—not only per-request prices.[1][2][8]

## Bring to work

**Retrieval boundary bake-off — medium effort.** Direct AgentCore fit. Freeze 50 current-information questions and compare Web Search, Web Answer, and the current retrieval stack on coverage, freshness, citation alignment, injection failures, p95 latency, and cost per supported answer.[1]

**Runtime version control — low effort.** Direct AgentCore fit. Inventory runtime generations, pin `platformVersion`, replay one representative workload on V1 and V2, and document rollback before migrating existing runtimes.[2][3]

**MCP hostile-repository regression — medium effort.** Direct Gateway/runtime fit. Patch exact versions, then test hostile `.git/config`, alternate object stores, symlinks or junctions, redirects, IPv6, and private-address access in isolation.[5][6]

**Decision calibration pilot — medium effort.** Transferable to Bedrock routing and escalation. Label 500 cases and compare calibration error, false automation, abstention, latency, and cost with the current generative classifier.[8][7]

## Watchouts

- AgentCore Web Search is regional and usage-priced; source trust and downstream claim validation remain application responsibilities.[1]
- AWS runtime startup and memory figures are vendor measurements under stated conditions, not workload guarantees.[2][3]
- MCP v2.4.0 still documents residual Windows junction and race limitations; read-only naming is not a security boundary.[5][6]
- Google’s Decisions API is v1beta, and OpenAI Agents SDK v0.24.0-alpha.7 is prerelease. Keep both out of irreversible production control paths until evaluated.[8][9][7]
